P07-001.challenge_claim: The row's undigited universal denial of any divine-speech frame inside its span is contested by the divine-utterance authentication formula standing at its third verse — the very formula cited at 22:25 in this same range as an oracle-closing signature — and that same verse is the row's one undisclosed seg site.
P07-001.grounds: The defects are real but the headline framing overstates the first one, and one digit's object is unnamed. WHAT THE BYTES SHOW. “כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה” stands at MT 24:3 at byte tier, and “כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר” closes MT 22:25 at byte tier; across the two verses the relation is SKELETON tier only, since the verb forms differ. CORRECTION TO THE FRAMING: the row's denial is not simply false. It denies a massa header, a hoy onset and a divine-speech frame, and every enumerated census returns ZERO in this chapter — no verse-initial massa header, no hoy onset, no koh-amar site, no postpositive signature, and no amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency anywhere in ch 24. Against the frame classes the device spine enumerates, the denial holds. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is enough. (a) The denial is a universal carrying no digit-bearing sweep beside it, which is the one thing a universal in row prose must have. (b) MT 24:3 carries an undisclosed in-span divine-utterance authentication signal whose class the NEIGHBOURING row in this same cluster treats as evidence, closing that oracle on its twin — so the range applies two weights to one class with nothing reconciling them, and 24:3's possible closing function at 24:3|24:4 is never weighed. (c) The one in-span seg object, 2 segs at MT 24:3, count-only and single-witness, is undisclosed although the row engages the mark layer and the same object is disclosed at MT 22:24, 23:1, 23:13 and 23:17 elsewhere in this range — a real symmetry gap. DIGIT-OBJECT DEFECT IN THE CHALLENGE, new: the sweep is cited as '10 verses book-wide' immediately after the fuller formula is quoted, but 10 is the count for the broader divine-name-plus-utterance-verb adjacency; the quoted formula itself returns 4 verses at skeleton tier (MT 1:2, 22:25, 24:3, 25:8). The digit is right for an object the challenge does not name — the blend the count discipline bars. Credits confirmed: the remnant claim is exact and correctly class-split — the verb-family members stand at MT 24:6 (“אֱנ֖וֹשׁ”) and MT 24:12 (“נִשְׁאַ֥ר”) and at no other verse in the span, held apart from the noun, the collective noun and the personal name sharing the root — though it is carried by an unpointed mention while listed as a substrate signal, so it does not meet the pointed-splice bar that listing implies. The parashah statement is true: the inventory returns 0 petuchah and 0 setumah inside 24:1-13, and the petuchah closing the preceding unit at MT 23:18 is correctly keyed and typed. The boundary is safe on independent grounds: the other lens re-derived MT 24:3 as a candidate internal seam and found no addressee or scene shift accompanying it.
P07-001.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: give the universal denial its digit-bearing sweep and name each census object — 0 verse-initial massa headers, 0 hoy onsets, 0 koh-amar sites, 0 postpositive signatures and 0 amar-plus-YHWH adjacencies in this chapter; test = every universal in the row stands beside a digit-bearing sweep that names its object and unit. (2) device_notes: disclose the authentication formula at MT 24:3 as an in-span divine-utterance signal, with its tier named (byte at its own verse; skeleton against its twin) and the sweep object named, and state why it does not close the unit at 24:3|24:4; test = the test that killed the original, namely that the same formula class is not treated as oracle-closing evidence at one verse in this range and as nothing at another without a stated ground. (3) device_notes: disclose the seg object at MT 24:3 (2 segs, single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position); test = the span-relevant seg-disclosure symmetry sweep over 24:1-13 finds nothing undisclosed. (4) device_notes: raise the remnant mention to a pointed splice from source bytes with its tier named, since it is carried as a substrate signal; test = every substrate-keyed claim is carried by a pointed splice that re-collates at the tier it names.

P07-002.challenge_claim: The row opens on a bare third-person-plural pronoun whose antecedent lies outside its span, leaving an anaphoric dependency straddling its own opening seam undisclosed; a supporting statement about the enumerated sung-praise sites is inaccurate as written; the divine-title key leaves a compound stack unnamed; and the setumah is cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key.
P07-002.grounds: Three strands verify; one is byte-false as charged. STRAND 1, upheld and the substantive one: MT 24:14 opens “הֵ֛מָּה”, an independent third-person-plural pronoun with no antecedent anywhere inside 24:14-15; the referent is supplied by the gleaning image closing the preceding verse, “כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת” at MT 24:13 (byte tier), which sits outside this row's span, and both witnesses read the pronoun as resumptive — the staged WEB text renders “These shall lift up their voice.” at web:Isa.24.14. The dependency is byte-true and argues continuity across this row's own opening seam, yet the rival sentence disputes only the far seam at 24:16 and the opening seam is left unargued. STRAND 2, upheld and confirmed against the controlled vocabulary itself: the row's prose states that the enumerated sung-praise sites 'begin at Isa.25.1'. They do not — the enumeration opens with a chapter-12 unit and only then reaches 25:1, so the parenthetical is false as written. It is also a register breach on its own: the sentence cites the governing strategy inside row prose, where the register purge bars strategy references outright, and the fix is to delete the apparatus rather than correct the verse number. STRAND 3, upheld: the divine-title key names the bare tetragrammaton, present twice in the span as a bare title, but MT 24:15 also carries the compound stack “שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” — a different count-object, unnamed. STRAND 4, REFUTED as charged: the setumah at MT 24:15 IS cited under the MT key in the row's own evidence refs, with the single-witness qualifier attached, so it is not 'cited under a translation-side prefix rather than the MT key'. The residual defect is smaller and different — the mark PROSE in device_notes carries a bare verse reference, which the convention reads as translation-side, while the evidence ref is correct; that is a prose-consistency slip, not a witness misattribution. Credits confirmed: the imperative form-class claim holds — “כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה” at MT 24:15 is read as a plural imperative by both witnesses, argued the sanctioned way since the staged extract carries no morphology layer — and the operative-category deviation for applying the sung-praise label to a two-verse summons carries the one-sentence disclosure the category law requires.
P07-002.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) device_notes: disclose the anaphoric dependency — the bare 3mp pronoun opening MT 24:14 taking its referent from the gleaning image closing MT 24:13, outside the span — as cross-seam cohesion, and state the warrant that survives it; test = a byte-true dependency straddling the row's own opening seam is disclosed before the seam is claimed. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: extend the rival to the opening seam, not only the far seam at 24:16; test = the rival addresses the seam the disclosed cohesion actually threatens. (3) boundary_rationale: delete the strategy-citing parenthetical outright — both because the claim is false, the enumeration opening at a chapter-12 unit rather than at 25:1, and because the register bars strategy references in row prose — and carry the category deviation on the bytes alone in the device_notes disclosure; test = no row field cites the governing strategy, and every surviving claim reproduces from the row's own bytes. (4) observed_substrate_signals and device_notes: name the compound title stack at MT 24:15 as its own count-object alongside the bare title, and make the mark prose carry the same MT key the evidence ref already uses; test = each divine-name digit names which object it counts, and mark references are keyed to the Masoretic witness in prose as well as in refs.

P07-003.challenge_claim: OL: the closing seam rests on a tier-3 single-witness mark alone — the tier-1 day-formula onset standing at the very next verse, the same onset treated as a driver at 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15 in this range, is neither quoted nor referenced, so the close is formally undriven. LF: the rejected-alternative disclosure names only the narrower 'own row for v.16' rival and omits a broader one, a recurring inhabitants-of-the-earth idiom tying 24:17-20 back to the chapter's own opening.
P07-003.grounds: Both items land and they are DISTINCT — opposite ends of the row, and of opposite valence. OL's, upheld and decisive: the row's stated ground for stopping at 24:20 is a setumah at that verse, an object campaign policy bars from driving any boundary, while MT 24:21 opens “וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” at byte tier — verse-initial, the sole day-formula site in this chapter, and the identical onset the neighbouring rows in this same range treat as a tier-1 driver at MT 22:20, 22:25 and 23:15. Neither the formula nor the verse carrying it appears anywhere in the row's prose or in its evidence refs, and the prose describes 24:17-20 as sustained imagery without saying why the sequence stops. The defect cuts in the row's favour: curing it REPLACES the barred tier-3 ground with the strongest tier-1 signal available, so the boundary is not in doubt — only its stated warrant. LF's, upheld in substance but REFINED in tier: the inhabitants idiom is real but it is not one recurrence at one tier. “יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ” at MT 24:1 and “יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ” at MT 24:5 match at accent_stripped (skeleton “ישביה”); the plural construct “אֶ֔רֶץ” at MT 24:6 is a different form (skeleton “ארץ”); and the load-bearing link for LF's rival, “יוֹשֵׁ֥ב” at MT 24:17, is a plene singular (skeleton “יושב”) that fails skeleton identity with ALL of them — the plene-versus-defective and singular-versus-plural hazard class. The four are the only yoshev-family sites in the chapter. So the rival is a lemma-level observation, not a tier-grounded recurrence, and 'lexical tier' is not one of the four sanctioned tiers; the omission is real, the strength claimed for it is not. NEW FINDING, unengaged by the row and by BOTH lenses: a second-person-masculine-singular addressee marker stands at MT 24:17 — “עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ” — and both witnesses read it as address, the staged WEB text rendering “Fear, the pit, and the snare are on you who inhabit the earth.” at web:Isa.24.17, while MT 24:18-20 revert to third-person description. That address sits at the exact internal junction 24:16|24:17 where the row asserts the treachery clause 'threads without a fresh scene marker' into the terror imagery. An addressee marker is a tier-1 class under the evidence policy, and the row's continuity claim is never tested against it. Credits confirmed: the hardest trap in the span is handled right — the exclamation at MT 24:16 is correctly identified as the distinct lexeme and never blended with the woe-series onset word; the treachery run is byte-true; the mid-verse turn from reported song to personal cry is held open rather than decided; the layout fold at that verse is real and correctly denied evidentiary weight. Disclosure inside the span is otherwise complete: setumah at MT 24:20 and at MT 24:15, and the inventories return 0 seg sites, 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 special-letter segs in 24:16-20, none of which the row claims. Medium, OL's severity, carries the row.
P07-003.remedy: Author work order, four edits, no boundary change. (1) boundary_rationale and boundary_evidence_refs: state the closing warrant on the tier-1 day-formula onset opening MT 24:21, quoted as a pointed splice with the verse added to the refs, and demote the setumah at MT 24:20 to what it is — tier-3 single-witness corroboration, never the ground; test = the test that killed the original, namely that no seam in the row rests on a parashah mark alone, and the same onset class is not a driver at three verses in this range and absent from the reasoning at a fourth. (2) strongest_rejected_alternative: add the broader rival — that 24:17-20 resumes the chapter's opening judgment idiom rather than continuing as one voice with the 24:16 lament — with its tier named honestly as a lemma-level observation across MT 24:1, 24:5, 24:6 and 24:17 whose forms differ at every collate tier, not as a byte-true or skeleton-true recurrence; test = every recurrence offered in the row names a sanctioned tier and reproduces at it, and a rival is not credited with strength its tier does not carry. (3) boundary_rationale: test the internal continuity claim at 24:16|24:17 against the 2ms addressee marker standing at MT 24:17 — argue why the material threads on despite an address entering there, or disclose the tension; test = the row's strongest internal counterevidence is quoted and answered rather than left unstated, form class argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. (4) Because the closing driver changes, re-derive observed_substrate_signals and confidence against the corrected warrant. The 24:16 voice-slide construal stays held at reduced confidence and is not decided here; any respan is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption.

P07-005.challenge_claim: The decisive closing-seam ground - a person and addressee shift between Isa.25.5 and Isa.25.6 - is asserted from the English rendering with no Hebrew form quoted on either side of the seam, and the front seam is crossed undisclosed by the exalt/height root that the preceding unit's own object supplies; separately the rationale points at a governing planning document as authority for the site.
P07-005.grounds: Two of the three arms hold, the third does not, and the severity is set too low. ARM 1 (upheld): the row's whole closing warrant is a person/addressee shift at the Isa.25.5 | Isa.25.6 seam, and the row's only pointed splice sits at oshb:Isa.25.1 - no Hebrew is quoted on either side of the seam it calls decisive. The claim is byte-TRUE and unengaged: second-person address runs unbroken through the span (oshb:Isa.25.2 שַׂ֤מְתָּ, oshb:Isa.25.3 יְכַבְּד֣וּךָ and יִירָאֽוּךָ, oshb:Isa.25.4 הָיִ֨יתָ, all byte tier) and closes on תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier), which the English reads “you will bring down the noise of strangers” (web:Isa.25.5), while oshb:Isa.25.6 opens וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (byte tier), putting the divine name in as explicit third-person subject - “Yahweh of Armies will make all peoples a feast” (web:Isa.25.6). The engagement mandate for boundary-relevant Hebrew claims is breached at the row's own decisive edge. ARM 2 (upheld, and under-weighted by the challenge): the rationale asserts its site as 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' - a governing-document authority claim inside boundary_rationale, which the register bar forbids in row prose in every field. The challenge relegates this to a trailing sentence; it is in fact the row's most concrete and most mechanically curable defect - and the same breach class at Isa.25.10-Isa.25.12 in this cluster is carried at medium. ARM 3 (refuted as a defect, retained as an observation): the exalt/height link between אֲרֽוֹמִמְךָ֙ (oshb:Isa.25.1, byte tier) and צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier) is NOT byte-true and not even a contiguous consonantal match - swept per attested spelling the mem-prefixed spelling stands at 13 verses book-wide and 4 in chs 23-27 (sweep: 4 verses - oshb:Isa.24.4, oshb:Isa.24.18, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.26.5) and the bare spelling at 7 book-wide and 2 here (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.23.4, oshb:Isa.25.1); the challenge's own digits verify exactly. The cross-seam cohesion rule binds byte-true devices straddling a row's own seam; a root-level echo at two different spellings is a disclosure courtesy, not a rule breach, and cannot carry severity on its own. Mark layer is correct as both primaries say: PE after oshb:Isa.24.23 and PE after oshb:Isa.25.5 bracket the span exactly, types unconflated, single-witness disclosed, and no mark falls inside Isa.25.1-Isa.25.5 (tier-3, absence not used either way).
P07-005.remedy: boundary_rationale: (a) delete the clause 'the strategy's own enumerated first-person praise site' outright - the site must be argued from this row's own bytes and nothing else; (b) add pointed splices on BOTH sides of the closing seam - תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier) and וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier) - with the form-class label held as a byte-checkable claim, since no morphology layer is available. Optional in device_notes: one sentence disclosing the exalt/height echo to oshb:Isa.24.21 as root-level per attested spelling, explicitly NOT byte-identical. No boundary change is proposed and none is needed. TESTS the cure must pass: the register scan finds no governing-document or planning-file reference in any field; every Hebrew run in the row re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse; the closing-seam sentence names a tier for every form it labels.

P07-006.challenge_claim: The row makes a demonstrative mountain-phrase its identifying frame without disclosing that the same phrase recurs on the far side of its own closing seam and without naming the tier at which the far site matches; and the divine-name object at Isa.25.8 goes unnamed while only the hosts-title is engaged.
P07-006.grounds: The tier finding is exactly right and is the real defect; the 'runs through' framing and the divine-name arm are not. VERIFIED: בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה stands byte-identical at oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 (sweep: 2 verses at byte tier) and recurs at oshb:Isa.25.10 as בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה - the accents differ, so the third site matches only at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses at those tiers, 2 at byte). The row makes the phrase its identifying frame ('matching בָּהָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier)') and discloses neither the in-span repetition at oshb:Isa.25.7 nor the recurrence past its own closing edge nor the tier drop at that far site - and the campaign standard requires the tier named on EVERY recurrence claim. CORRECTION to the framing: the phrase does not 'run oshb:Isa.25.6 through oshb:Isa.25.10'. oshb:Isa.25.8 and oshb:Isa.25.9 carry no occurrence at any tier, so the signal is three sites with a two-verse gap, and no site sits on either side of the row's own 25:8 | 25:9 seam. It argues a mountain-motif band reaching two verses past the row's close, which is a real disclosure obligation, but it is weaker than a device straddling the seam itself. REFUTED arm: אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה does stand byte-true at oshb:Isa.25.8, but the row makes no divine-name count claim anywhere - it names a title as span texture - and the count-object discipline bites on digits and swept objects, not on an obligation to enumerate every title present in a span. This is an observation, not a defect. Sound as the challenge says: בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֨וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח (oshb:Isa.25.8, byte tier) answers the waw-prefixed verb opening oshb:Isa.25.7 in-span; the back-seam opener וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.25.9) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse, byte AND skeleton tier); PE after oshb:Isa.25.5 and PE after oshb:Isa.25.8 match the inventory under the right type.
P07-006.remedy: device_notes: add one sentence disclosing that the row's identifying mountain-phrase repeats in-span at oshb:Isa.25.7 (byte tier) and recurs beyond the row's close at oshb:Isa.25.10 at accent_stripped / skeleton tier only (sweep: 2 verses byte, 3 verses accent_stripped), and state that the motif band is not treated as a boundary driver. Do NOT restate it as a continuous run and do not add a divine-name enumeration. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the recurrence sentence names a tier and a digit with its unit; a byte-tier sweep of the cited phrase returns exactly oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 and an accent_stripped sweep adds oshb:Isa.25.10 and nothing else.

P07-007.challenge_claim: LF: the applied unit_type is given to a projected communal confession without the one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category rule requires. OL: a one-verse row is cut out of the middle of a three-verse anaphoric chain with no disclosure at either edge, and its back seam is crossed by a causal particle that subordinates the following clause to this verse.
P07-007.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one - LF's is a category-disclosure defect in device_notes, OL's is a seam-engagement defect in boundary_rationale. LF UPHELD as written: the applied value's operative line is the promise/comfort oracle, and this row's own literature_type_guess calls the verse a communal confession formula - quoted retrospective acclamation by the people (וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא, oshb:Isa.25.9, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse). The operative-category law admits any closed-vocabulary value wherever the row's bytes carry that form, but ONLY with a one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes; this row's device_notes carries none, while the Isa.26.7-Isa.26.19 row in this cluster does supply one for the same law. Refinement of LF's framing only: the trigger is the mismatch with the operative DESCRIPTION, not absence from the enumerated example list (the adjacent Isa.25.6-Isa.25.8 row is equally off-list yet squarely promise/comfort and needs no disclosure), and LF's suggested sung-praise alternative is weak - the verse is reported speech, not a sung unit - so the defect is the missing sentence, not the label chosen. OL REFINED. Its second arm is byte-true and is the stronger finding: oshb:Isa.25.10 opens כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ (byte tier), a causal particle binding the following clause back across this row's closing edge, and the rationale argues that cut only forward (a subject narrowing to a named foreign power at 25:10) without ever engaging the particle pointing backward. Its first arm is materially misframed: the mountain-phrase sites are oshb:Isa.25.6 and oshb:Isa.25.7 (byte) and oshb:Isa.25.10 (accent_stripped / skeleton), so this row is NOT 'precisely the single verse wedged between the second and third sites' - oshb:Isa.25.8 lies between them too, and the phrase occurs nowhere inside this row. The chain brackets a two-verse gap spanning two rows; it does not isolate this one. Correct in both packets: PE after oshb:Isa.25.8 is cited under the right type as single-witness, and the inventory records no mark after oshb:Isa.25.9, as the row implies.
P07-007.remedy: (1) device_notes: add the one-sentence operative-category deviation disclosure for the applied unit_type, arguing the value from this verse's own bytes (quoted future acclamation under its own reported-speech frame) - one sentence, no label change proposed. (2) boundary_rationale: engage the closing seam in BOTH directions - splice כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ (oshb:Isa.25.10, byte tier) and state why the causal particle does not bind Isa.25.10 into this verse's unit, or record the rival honestly and re-check the confidence band. Do NOT write the mountain-phrase chain up as a continuous run; if it is disclosed, cite it as sites with tiers. No respan is proposed here; any actual boundary change is a proposal for boss adoption, never author work. TESTS: device_notes contains exactly one deviation sentence naming the applied value; the closing-seam sentence carries a pointed splice from oshb:Isa.25.10 that re-collates at byte tier; no sentence asserts a continuous phrase run across oshb:Isa.25.8-Isa.25.9.

P07-008.challenge_claim: LF: the row's own notes name the shared staged verification apparatus directly ('per the toolkit's fold guidance'), a barred staged-file reference in row prose. OL: the layout datum the row discloses is misdescribed - the English continuation paragraph is a mid-verse break inside Isa.25.10 at the Moab pivot, not a fold onto Isa.25.9 - and the byte-identical clause pair straddling the row's closing seam is undisclosed.
P07-008.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT defects sitting in the same two fields. LF UPHELD: device_notes reads 'per the toolkit's fold guidance', naming the shared staged verification apparatus in row prose - the register bar forbids tool and staged-file names in EVERY field, and the sentence adds nothing the fold disclosure does not already carry. OL UPHELD, and byte-confirmed from the source layout rather than from the derived map: the English opens a paragraph BEFORE web:Isa.25.9, and web:Isa.25.10 carries its single continuation paragraph INTERNALLY, immediately before “Moab will be trodden down in his place” (web:Isa.25.10) - i.e. the break lands exactly on the Moab pivot the row uses as its own content ground. The row states the opposite twice (a fold 'onto' 25:9 in boundary_rationale, a fold 'linking' 25:9 and 25:10 in device_notes) and its strongest_rejected_alternative rests on that description, so a tier-4 datum that can never drive is nonetheless misreported in a load-bearing field, and the row argues against a layout signal that does not exist while ignoring the one that does. OL's cross-seam arm also verifies: עַד עָפָֽר is BYTE-identical at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5), one on each side of this row's back edge; הֵשַׁ֥ח / הֵשַׁח֙ match at accent_stripped tier at those same two verses (the further skeleton hit at oshb:Isa.25.11 is the swimming lexeme, a different object, as the challenge says); and מִשְׂגַּ֣ב / נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה share the sgv skeleton, which stands at 9 verses book-wide with only these two in chs 23-27. That is a byte-true device straddling the row's own seam and it is answered nowhere. NEW FINDING (cross-check): the LF packet verified this same fold as 'confirmed against the staged verse map' and accepted the row's description - the existence digit was reproduced with the wrong count-object, which is the defect class the peer round exists to catch. Correct as written in the row: the opening splice properly includes the governing particle כִּֽי תָנ֥וּחַ; the ketiv/qere note at oshb:Isa.25.10 is disclosed single-witness and the quotation stops well before the staged doubled pair; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.25.12 matches the inventory under the right type.
P07-008.remedy: (1) device_notes: delete the clause 'per the toolkit's fold guidance' - the fold disclosure stands on its own. (2) boundary_rationale AND device_notes: restate the layout datum correctly in one place only - the continuation paragraph is INTERNAL to web:Isa.25.10, falling before “Moab will be trodden down in his place” (web:Isa.25.10) - and keep it labelled tier-4 and non-driving; then rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative so it no longer rests on the false 'fold onto Isa.25.9' description (the content pivot to the named foreign power already carries it). (3) SEAM-PAIR EDIT, one edit across this row and the following one: disclose the עַד עָפָֽר bracket as byte-identical at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.25.12 | oshb:Isa.26.5) with the heshach pair named at accent_stripped tier and the sgv pair at skeleton tier, and say why it does not bind the two rows into one. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: the register scan finds no tool or staged-file name in any field; the layout sentence, read against the source paragraphing, places the break inside web:Isa.25.10 and not at the 25:9 | 25:10 join; a byte-tier sweep of the cited two-word run returns exactly oshb:Isa.25.12 and oshb:Isa.26.5; the same disclosure appears on both sides of the seam pair.

P07-009.challenge_claim: The closing seam and the rejected alternative both rest solely on the English translation's quotation punctuation, which has no counterpart in the Hebrew, and the row's two named devices are asserted without a single Hebrew form quoted for either; the front seam is also crossed undisclosed by a byte-identical clause pair.

P07-010.grounds: The two packets OVERLAP on one arm (the undisclosed ketiv/qere) and OL adds two arms the other packet did not reach. All three are real. The row's blanket claim is nevertheless TRUE at the second mark: 2ms address stands on both sides of the break after oshb:Isa.26.11 (oshb:Isa.26.12 פָּעַ֥לְתָּ, oshb:Isa.26.13 זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ and בְּךָ֖, byte tier), and the challenge correctly scoped its finding to 'the first one'. Note the marks stay tier-3 weak and cannot drive an edge in either direction; the defect is the false reason, not the decision. ARM 2, OL only, correctly HELD rather than asserted: the closing criterion (a voice commanding the community, said to begin only at 26:20) is already present inside the row's final verse - הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier; the two runs are each unique in the book, sweep: 1 verse each), rendered “Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust” (web:Isa.26.19). With no morphology layer staged this is a form-class reading, and the challenge flags it as held; the point stands as stated - the criterion as written does not separate 26:19 from 26:20. ARM 3, BOTH packets, same defect: the row quotes “Come, my people, enter into your rooms” (web:Isa.26.20) as its close-boundary evidence with no ketiv/qere disclosure anywhere, while oshb:Isa.26.20 carries TWO notes staged as the doubled pairs דלתיך דְּלָתְךָ֖ and יעבור יַעֲבָר (single-witness); the adjacent row quoting the same verse does disclose both. (3) SEAM-PAIR EDIT with the following row, one edit: add the ketiv/qere disclosure for oshb:Isa.26.20 (two notes, single-witness, quotation stopping before both staged pairs) AND note that the English clause quoted renders the plural, aligning with the ketiv - or stop quoting that clause. P07-011.challenge_claim: The closing-seam ground names a frame formula in the next verse without ever quoting it, and the root repetition that hooks Isa.26.21 straight into Isa.27.1 across that seam is undisclosed; the front-edge criterion is also already present one verse earlier.
P07-011.grounds: The engagement arm is upheld; the 'nowhere answered' framing of the cohesion arm is overstated and the tier is not what the wording implies. REFINED, cohesion arm: the hook is real but weaker and differently tiered than stated. This row's closing word is לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and the next verse continues יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier); the two forms are NOT byte-identical to each other - they share the consonantal skeleton only, which stands at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), while the fuller construction the challenge cites stands at exactly 3 verses at accent_stripped / skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses - oshb:Isa.23.17, oshb:Isa.24.21, oshb:Isa.27.1), reopening the frame that opened this cluster at יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.24.21, byte tier). And the row does not leave the continuity wholly unanswered: its rationale states in terms that the verse 'continues without a further addressee change into the leviathan judgment of Isa.27.1' and rests the cut on the fresh formula plus the mark layer. What is missing is the Hebrew-level catchword and its tier, not the acknowledgement. The challenge's front-edge point verifies and is correctly held as a form-class reading: הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר (oshb:Isa.26.19, byte tier) already reverses the direction of address one verse before the row opens, so the row's distinguishing criterion does not by itself separate the two verses. Correct as written and worth recording: the ketiv/qere handling here is exact - the splice stops at וּֽסְגֹ֥ר, before both staged pairs, with the doubling disclosed single-witness; SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.19 and after oshb:Isa.26.21 are cited under the right type.

P07-012.challenge_claim: The one-verse unit's onset and both its mark disclosures are byte-true, but a divine-visitation catchword runs across both of its seams undisclosed, and the onset formula it leans on is a large class carried without a digit.
P07-012.grounds: Both arms point at something real; the first names the wrong count-object and the second reaches past this row's own burden. ARM 1, REFINED - the object is blended. The three sites verify in the bytes: לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21), יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1) and פֶּ֚ן יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.3), all byte tier in their cited verses, with the root skeleton at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses) exactly as the challenge says. But calling all three 'a divine-visitation chain' blends two speech-roles into one swept object, which the count-discipline bars: at oshb:Isa.26.21 and oshb:Isa.27.1 the visiting agent is the divine name itself, while oshb:Isa.27.3 is a negative-purpose clause inside first-person divine speech in which the speaker is the vineyard's KEEPER and the visiting agent is someone else - “Lest anyone damage it” (web:Isa.27.3). CORRECTED FINDING, and it is sharper than the original at the back edge: יִפְקֹ֣ד is BYTE-identical at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses - oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3), so a byte-true lexical recurrence does cross this row's closing edge and is undisclosed - but it must be cited as that lexical form, not as a visitation chain. At the front edge the link to לִפְקֹ֛ד is skeleton-level only, not byte. The 'straddling BOTH edges' wording also skips that oshb:Isa.27.2 carries no occurrence at any tier. ARM 2, part UPHELD, part out of scope. Upheld: the row's sole onset driver is the day formula and it carries no digit and no swept object anywhere in the row, although the class is large and unevenly distributed across tiers - the byte-tier form the row quotes, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא, stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses at byte tier - oshb:Isa.7.20, oshb:Isa.19.18, oshb:Isa.27.1), while the same formula at skeleton tier stands at 45 verses book-wide (sweep: 45 verses), and the challenge's 45-verse digit is correct for that object. The formula is also not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine, so its discriminating power is exactly the thing the row leaves unquantified - and the very next verse opens the same formula at accent_stripped tier (בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא, oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier in its own verse; the two openers differ in their accents, so they are NOT byte-identical to each other), which is the row's own seam. Out of scope: 'does not distinguish the bare form from the waw-prefixed long form used two rows later' compares this row against other rows' choices; that is a cross-row consistency question for the campaign, not a defect in this row's prose, and stating it positionally is itself barred register. Correct as the challenge concedes: every Hebrew run in the row matches its cited verse at byte tier, and SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.26.21 and after oshb:Isa.27.1 are correctly typed, correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness, and disclosed single-witness and non-driving (tier-3).
P07-012.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: give the onset formula a swept object and a digit at the tier quoted - the byte-tier form at 3 verses book-wide, or the formula class at skeleton tier at 45 verses book-wide, naming which - and state what distinguishes this onset from the identical bare formula opening the very next verse, since both cannot be onsets on the formula alone. (2) device_notes: add one sentence disclosing the byte-identical recurrence of יִפְקֹ֣ד at oshb:Isa.27.1 and oshb:Isa.27.3 (byte tier, sweep: 2 verses book-wide) across this row's closing edge, naming the lexical form as the object and noting that the two sites carry different speech-roles; the front-edge link to לִפְקֹ֛ד may be added as skeleton-level only, explicitly NOT byte. Do NOT write it up as a divine-visitation chain. No boundary change proposed. P07-013.challenge_claim: The song-frame identification at the onset verse and the close at 27:5 both rest on English rendering choices that the Hebrew of the cited verses does not carry; and the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew word order.
P07-013.grounds: All three arms verify, and the challenge is if anything too generous on the third. ARM 1: the onset verse carries no song lexeme at any tier. oshb:Isa.27.2 reads בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (byte tier) - six tokens, none of them the song noun or its cognate verb, which stand together at יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier, unique in the book at sweep: 1 verse) and whose consonantal skeleton stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses), the nearest being oshb:Isa.26.1 itself. The row nevertheless calls this 'a second, separate song frame' and its signal keys carry a song-announcement formula, so a frame class with a real instance one chapter earlier is imported into a verse whose bytes carry no such form. The construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ as an order to sing is defensible on its own, and the unit_type is not what is being challenged - the defect is a FORMULA claim asserted without the form present in the cited verse. ARM 2, the sharpest and most mechanically curable: the quote/gloss pairing inverts the Hebrew. The row pairs the English clause “In that day, sing to her,” (web:Isa.27.2) with the whole six-token run and then presents “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2) as a quotation INTRODUCED by that run - but כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), the words so rendered, are the THIRD and FOURTH tokens inside the very run cited, standing before the verb. The 'formula, then introduced quotation' sequencing exists only because the English reorders the clause; the full English is “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2). Quote/gloss parity is campaign law and the gloss must be re-cut. ARM 3: the close's first arm is where the English quotation mark falls - “Let him make peace with me.” (web:Isa.27.5) - and the pointed bytes of oshb:Isa.27.2 through oshb:Isa.27.5 carry letters and accents and no quotation delimitation at any tier, so that arm is a tier-4 rendering artifact and can never set an edge; the material inside the English quotation is itself first-person divine speech, which the delimiter does not track. ADDED, and it strengthens rather than softens the challenge: the second, byte-grounded arm of the close does NOT survive as stated either. The row argues a new opening at 27:6 from the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6) and quotes no Hebrew there at all. The bytes give הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), a bare participial form unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; the noun that makes it read as a dated formula is supplied by the translation. So both halves of this row's closing warrant are carried by the rendering. Correct as written: the two Hebrew runs the row does quote reach byte tier in their cited verses, the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.1 is cited under the right type as single-witness, the inventory records no further mark inside Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 as the row says, and the cross-part vineyard relation to Isa.5.1-Isa.5.7 is properly quarantined as typed metadata.
P07-013.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: re-cut the gloss so quote and Hebrew agree - either splice the onset's two tokens alone and gloss כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד separately in its own place in the run, or quote the whole run against the whole English clause “In that day, sing to her, “A pleasant vineyard!” (web:Isa.27.2); the introduced-quotation sequencing must go. (2) Replace the song-FRAME assertion with what the bytes support: an onset formula plus a construal of עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier), stated as a construal, with the song-announcement signal key dropped or re-keyed, since the formula's real instance is at oshb:Isa.26.1 and not here. (3) Re-warrant the closing edge from bytes: splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.27.6 to boundary_evidence_refs, and say what the form is (a bare participial onset, not a staged frame class); the English quotation mark may remain only as an explicitly tier-4, non-driving corroboration. No boundary change is proposed. TESTS: no field rests an edge on translation punctuation or on a noun the translation supplies; every English gloss maps to the Hebrew tokens actually inside the run it is paired with; every formula/frame claim names a form present in the cited verse's own bytes with its tier.

P07-014.challenge_claim: The row's load-bearing reason for overriding a marked internal break is a plural English pronoun that does not stand in either of the two verses it is claimed for, and a feminine-suffix chain reaching back across the row's own front seam is undisclosed; the onset is also called a fresh formula though it is a bare participial form.
P07-014.grounds: Two arms hold; the suffix-chain arm is byte-false as framed. ARM 1 UPHELD, and it is the load-bearing one: strongest_rejected_alternative sets aside a single-witness setumah recorded after MT 27:6 on the ground that 'the pronoun "them" opening Isa.27.7 has no antecedent besides Jacob and Israel named in Isa.27.6'. No such pronoun stands there. oshb:Isa.27.7 opens הַכְּמַכַּ֥ת (byte tier), an interrogative-comparative construction, and its suffixes are third masculine singular - מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ and הֲרֻגָ֖יו (byte tier) - while the English “Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them?” (web:Isa.27.7) renders them collectively and does not put 'them' at the head of the verse either. The referential conclusion may still be reachable from those 3ms forms, but the row quotes no Hebrew from 27:7-8 at all and never makes that argument, so a tier-3 mark is overridden on a ground available only in the rendering. ADDED PRECISION: the row's rationale extends one English 'them' across 'Isa.27.7-8', but the suffixes at oshb:Isa.27.8 are third feminine singular - בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (byte tier) - so a single pronoun is being carried over TWO different suffix classes. Held as a form-class reading, since no morphology layer is staged. ARM 2 REFUTED AS FRAMED: there is no 3fs chain 'straddling the 27:5 | 27:6 seam'. The feminine suffixes run oshb:Isa.27.2 (עַנּוּ לָֽהּ), oshb:Isa.27.3 (נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה) and oshb:Isa.27.4 (אֶפְשְׂעָ֥ה בָ֖הּ אֲצִיתֶ֥נָּה), all byte tier - and then STOP: oshb:Isa.27.5 carries first-person forms instead (יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה שָׁל֖וֹם לִ֑י, byte tier), oshb:Isa.27.6 carries no pronominal suffix at all, and oshb:Isa.27.7 is 3ms. They resume only at oshb:Isa.27.8, two verses past the seam. The real observation - a feminine object reappearing at 27:8 that may reach back to the vineyard - is worth disclosing, but it does not cross this row's front edge as a chain and cannot argue continuity there. ARM 3 UPHELD: הַבָּאִים֙ (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse) and is a bare participial form, not a member of the staged tier-1 frame spine; calling it 'a fresh formula' while quoting the English “In days to come, Jacob will take root” (web:Isa.27.6), which supplies the noun, labels a class the bytes do not carry. Correct as the challenge concedes: the two Hebrew runs the row quotes reach byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.6 and after oshb:Isa.27.11 are correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness. The row is already held at reduced confidence with its frontier flag set, which is the right posture for this stretch.
P07-014.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: rewrite the override on Hebrew ground or drop it. It must splice מַכֵּ֖הוּ הִכָּ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.27.7, byte tier) and name the suffix class as a byte-checkable, held form-class claim, and it must stop attributing one plural pronoun to 27:7 and 27:8 together, since בְּשַׁלְחָ֣הּ תְּרִיבֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.8, byte tier) is a different class; add oshb:Isa.27.7 and oshb:Isa.27.8 to boundary_evidence_refs. Keep the mark tier-3 weak and non-driving either way. (2) boundary_rationale: replace 'a fresh formula' with what the bytes give - splice הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) and describe it as a bare participial onset, noting that the dating noun is supplied by the rendering. P07-015.challenge_claim: The split of the two adjacent day-formula verses is defended by a generalized pattern claim with no digit and by importing a different device class, while the linking form shared by both onsets is never weighed; the long form stands in 13 verses book-wide and these two are its only adjacent pair.
P07-015.grounds: The disclosure residue is real but small, and two of the challenge's own load-bearing claims are byte-false. BYTE-FALSE 1 - the exclusivity claim: the waw-prefixed long onset stands at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 13 verses - oshb:Isa.7.18, 7.21, 7.23, 10.20, 10.27, 11.10, 11.11, 17.4, 22.20, 23.15, 24.21, 27.12, 27.13), and that set contains TWO adjacent pairs, not one: oshb:Isa.11.10 | oshb:Isa.11.11 as well as oshb:Isa.27.12 | oshb:Isa.27.13. 'These two are its only adjacent pair' does not survive the sweep it cites. BYTE-FALSE 2 - the identity claim: the two onsets are NOT the identical form at byte tier. וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13) each re-collate at byte tier in their own verse but differ from each other in their accents; they agree only at accent_stripped and skeleton tier. Calling them 'identical' is exactly the accent-blind framing the tier-disclosure standard exists to prevent. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is a low-grade disclosure gap rather than a warrant failure: the row carries no digit and no tier for the onset formula it makes its splitting ground, and the bare form it treats as a unit onset two rows earlier is a much larger object (sweep: 45 verses at skeleton tier) than the long form here, so two distinct spellings do sit under one undifferentiated signal key. REFINED on the massa arm: the header class IS a different object - exactly 10 verse-initial sites, bounding parent oracles, none of them in this chapter - so the analogy borrows warrant from a class the row is not using. But this is an appeal to analogy, not a blended sweep, so it is a warrant-strength defect rather than a count-discipline breach. Separately and more concretely, the same sentence appeals to what 'this campaign otherwise treats' - a governance-process appeal that row prose should not carry in any field. REFINED on the unweighed-counter-reading arm: the row DOES weigh the merge - its strongest_rejected_alternative is precisely that reading, and it notes the shared destination itself. What is genuinely missing is the grammatical arm, that the waw on both onsets is a sequencing form which reads at least as readily as one continuing announcement. Correct as written: the quoted run reaches byte tier, and the SAMEKH after oshb:Isa.27.11 and after oshb:Isa.27.12 are correctly typed, correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness, and disclosed single-witness and non-driving.
P07-015.remedy: (1) strongest_rejected_alternative: delete the appeal to campaign practice and to the header class; re-warrant the split from this row's own bytes - the two onsets agree at accent_stripped tier and differ at byte tier, each opens a distinct image, and a single-witness setumah stands between them (tier-3, non-driving) - and add one clause weighing the sequencing reading of the waw rather than leaving it unanswered. (2) boundary_rationale: give the onset formula a tier and a digit with its unit named (the long form at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier), and distinguish it from the bare form so the signal key is not carrying two spellings. No boundary change proposed. TESTS: no field appeals to campaign practice, a governing document, or a device class the row is not itself using; every recurrence claim names a tier and carries a digit with its unit; the word 'identical' appears only where a byte-tier collation supports it.

P07-016.challenge_claim: The row closes the book's 27:13|28:1 frame seam without quoting the frame form that makes it a seam, and explains the missing mark there with a generalization the mark inventory contradicts.
P07-016.grounds: Both arms verify exactly. ARM 1: the closing seam is argued from the parent grouping ('the closing verse of its book-level parent grouping, so this row's own close is fixed by that larger seam') and from the row's own onset, never from the following verse's bytes. web:Isa.28.1 appears as a bare reference with no oshb: counterpart anywhere in the row, and the form that makes 28:1 a seam - the verse-initial ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier), a member of the 20-site verse-initial woe inventory - is never quoted. A frame-based seam claim owes the frame form and its role in the cited verse's own bytes. The asymmetry is visible across the seam pair: the Isa.28.1-Isa.28.13 row on the other side of this very join DOES quote that form byte-true. ARM 2: the row states that no mark follows Isa.27.13 and that this is 'expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. The absence itself is TRUE - the parashah inventory records no petuchah or setumah at MT 27:13 - but the explanation is contradicted by the inventory. Of the eight verses that close a parent grouping in this architecture, FIVE carry a mark - petuchah at MT 12:6, MT 35:10 and MT 39:8; setumah at MT 48:22 and MT 55:13 - and only MT 1:1, MT 27:13 and MT 66:24 do not. Every digit in the challenge checks out. So a tier-3 absence is given explanatory work on a layer where absence is never evidence in either direction, and the generalization it is given is false besides. CLARIFICATION, not a defect: MT 27:13 does carry one paseq seg (single-witness, count-only). That is a different layer with no symmetry obligation, so its non-mention is not a gap - but the row's flat 'no mark in the inventory' wording should not be read as covering it. Correct as written: the row's own onset run and its trumpet run both match oshb:Isa.27.13 at byte tier, and the setumah after MT 27:12 at the front seam is correctly typed and correctly keyed to the Hebrew witness.
P07-016.remedy: (1) boundary_rationale: splice ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier) into the closing-seam sentence, name its role as a verse-initial woe onset opening the next series, and add oshb:Isa.28.1 to boundary_evidence_refs, so the seam is engaged in the bytes on both sides of the join. The parent-grouping close may stay as corroboration but cannot be the only warrant. (2) device_notes: cut the explanatory clause 'which is expected since it is the book's own frame-seam verse'. State the absence flatly as a single-witness, tier-3 observation that is not treated as evidence in either direction, or drop the sentence entirely. No boundary change proposed - the seam is fixed architecture. TESTS: the seam claim carries a pointed splice from oshb:Isa.28.1 that re-collates at byte tier; the reference mirror shows oshb:Isa.28.1 present in boundary_evidence_refs; no field assigns explanatory or structural meaning to the absence of a parashah mark.
